Small instructions. Useful bit tricks. A five-stage RISC-V core you can program in C, inspect in assembly, and test before it ever reaches an FPGA.

01

A packet-sized introduction.

RISCue is a custom RISC-V implementation—not an ARM core. Its instruction set follows standard encodings, so ordinary RISC-V tools can target it. The repository's software profile tells GCC exactly which extensions are available.

Compile the code you want to write.

Use C for packet parsing and control. Drop into assembly where a bit-level operation is clearer. Zbs handles individual bits; Zbb adds useful operations such as rotates and bit counting; Zbc provides carry-less multiplication.

No self-modifying code is needed for this CRC routine. The instruction bexti extracts the feedback bit directly.

Protection is a deliberate choice.

The default pipeline uses triplicated state. An experimental parity/replay variant shares the same external interface, with protected architectural state and conservative fail-stop handling around uncertain memory effects. Register-file protection is selected independently.

This is development RTL and simulation evidence. Flight qualification, protocol compliance, physical implementation, and a Tiny Tapeout fit are separate work.

02

A CRC, without a custom instruction.

This routine uses the standard Zbs bexti instruction to select the feedback bit and Zbb zext.h to keep the state at 16 bits. It is intentionally readable rather than maximally optimized.

crc16.S · RV32 + Zbb + ZbsLEAF FUNCTION
__ASSEMBLY__
a0 points to bytes · a1 is length · a2 is the seed
Returns the 16-bit CRC in a0. No hardware CRC block is required.
TRY THE ALGORITHM

Type a packet payload.

The calculation below runs in your browser. The assembly result is checked separately in the recorded RTL simulation.

0x29B19 bytes
CRC-16/IBM-3740 (also called CCITT-FALSE)
Polynomial 0x1021 · initial state 0xFFFF
Input/output reflection off · final XOR 0x0000

The named check vector is 123456789 → 0x29B1. A protocol's polynomial, seed, reflection, byte order, and coverage must match its specification. This example does not claim SpaceWire or CCSDS conformance.

Have a look at SharpTestBench.
SharpTestBench is the companion C# hardware-testing framework. Its documented backends include Icarus and Verilator, with test results and VCD waveform artifacts. Build repeatable checks around packets, bus transactions, and error cases.
